outputs.prompt: Create one wide, horizontal story illustration for the French Silent Hill 3 chronicle “Naître deux fois”, set in the commercial 2003 game. Use the two supplied original gameplay images as visual references for Heather's physical appearance, clothing, shopping center and diner. An entirely new cinematic frame establishing the ordinary Central Square Shopping Center at closing time: seen from just outside a small warm dark diner, Heather pauses in profile beside a booth, a slim figure with short disheveled blond hair, off-white sleeveless hooded vest over orange top, short dark olive-green skirt, brown boots. Flat amber slats of late light from the venetian blinds stripe her vest and an empty wood table; the mall's unlit hallway is partly visible past the doorway. Portrait and shoulders small enough to retain the atmosphere but readable; put the subject in the upper/central-right half. Restrained cinematic grain and detailed early-2000s materials, painterly physical light, scuffed wood, grey-green shadows and warmth in the blinds. An ordinary place just becoming unsettling. Wide 16:9 illustration, full bleed, opaque, no lettering, logos, captions, buttons, UI or watermark. A standalone illustrated chapter opening, not a screenshot replica.

outputs.prompt: Create one wide atmospheric aftermath illustration for the fan-made French Silent Hill 3 (2003) chronicle ending “Le dieu tombe, mais la mémoire reste.” The original gameplay frames are architectural and costume references: its aging dark wooden chapel, narrow altar, worn floorboards, vertical gold-amber stained glass, modest wax candles and Heather's short pale hair and ivory sleeveless hooded vest. Make a new, tranquil cinematic view from the empty pews toward the altar, with Heather seen small from behind near the right aisle quietly looking back, clearly the same young woman in an ivory sleeveless hooded vest and dark olive skirt. The altar and stained glass occupy the center-left. The warm amber window light grazes the scratched wood; a few dying candle flames appear against deep but readable olive-brown shadow. Intimate post-confrontation silence and memory. An interpretive ending to this game's chronicle, without specifying an official numbered ending. No creatures, bodies, symbols invented for the scene, weapons, lettering, HUD, watermark or borders. Wide horizontal 16:9, full bleed, opaque cinematic survival-horror illustration with fine film grain, ungraded neutral blacks and tactile textures.

outputs.prompt: Paint a widescreen cinematic narrative illustration of Henry Townshend's apartment 302 in Silent Hill 4: The Room (2004). Use both supplied retail gameplay images as exact room and chain references. Inside the narrow, modest apartment, the ordinary cream paneled front door is bound shut from the inside by an irregular network of heavy dark chains, protruding metal anchor plates and locks. The view is wide enough to include the little kitchen beside the entrance, off-white refrigerator and cupboards, muted plaster, worn floor, circular overhead lamp. In the left foreground a small, unobtrusive back view of Henry in his muted grey shirt faces the locked door; the chains and the geometry of the entrance are the central focus. Restrained, subdued grey-yellow daylight, documentary survival-horror composition and detailed worn domestic textures, tense and quiet. The frame is a new piece of concept illustration for a chapter prologue, not an official screenshot. Build around central visual elements that will survive wide responsive retakes. Opaque horizontal 16:9, no UI, titles, watermark, gore, added symbols or legible words.

outputs.prompt: Create one finished wide story-ending illustration for the Silent Hill 4: The Room (2004) chronicle “Les vingt-et-un sacrements”, whose own closing line is “La chaîne se tend jusqu’au dernier nom.” Use the supplied retail scenes solely to anchor the appearance of the exact chained door in apartment 302. Deliberately different from a room-establishing shot: a nearly perpendicular, intimate low-angle close view of two heavy blackened chain lengths stretched taut across the cream scuffed lower door panels and their original metal anchor brackets. Let the crossing links dominate the middle of the composition and cast thin slanting shadows across painted wood. A sliver of the familiar threshold is visible along the bottom. Cold, pale light on the metal rubbing points gives the image a still, unresolved finality. No person, handwritten text, victim number, monster, blood, trophy, opened door, or claim that any one retail ending happened. Physically grounded cinematic illustration, fine grain and restrained slate/sepia palette. Opaque landscape 16:9, no caption, title, HUD, edge frame or watermark.

outputs.prompt: Illustrate the opening of a narrative chapter in Silent Hill: Origins (the PSP game), 'Les miroirs de Travis'. Use the attached two game images as exact visual references for Travis Grady, the mirror mechanic and the institutional washroom fixtures. A new cinematic widescreen composition: Travis, in his worn baseball cap, faded brown-red checked flannel shirt and weathered quilted outdoor vest, stands at the side of a large ordinary wall mirror above a row of old white ceramic basins. His beam catches the dingy glass; the round patch of light inside the mirror reveals a faint rust-brown reflection of the same wall across from him. Seen three-quarter from behind, grounded and motionless with one hand near the sink, no face closeup. Feature the blue-green glazed square tiles and plain metal tap, specific to the original material. Light and geometry keep the left reflection and middle Travis readable. The bathroom feels old and uninhabited. Muted green-grey, very subtle warm reflected light, grounded cinematic survival-horror illustration, fine grain. Fully opaque landscape 16:9, full bleed, no HUD, lettering, other people, invented ritual marks or monsters. An opening illustration distinct from the reference screenshots.

outputs.prompt: Paint a 16:9 horizontal closing illustration for Silent Hill: Origins with the two retail objects shown. The FIRST attached picture from the PSP game's official strategy guide is the precise final outline of the assembled Flauros. Look straight at this tiny red triangular pyramid, resting on a broad, flat triangular base. Its top is a single sharp point. Its outer silhouette is one upright triangle with three corners in the camera view, widening all the way down to its lowest and broadest edge. Four small engraved triangular insert sections form a single complete face; there is an inverted triangular inset in the lower center WITHIN the outline. All four vertices belong to one tetrahedron, flat bottom against the table, no projecting point below the base. Leave a soft dull ruby-orange highlight along one inset to suggest the closing seam. Keep the screenshot's thin golden edges and dark-red panel finish; do not invent engraved eyes or magic glyphs. Second reference is the actual room 500 key with shabby brass tag and a simple short household key. Place the small pyramid to the left of center, the tag and key farther right, on one plain worn dark tabletop, a subtle symbolic recollection of Travis’s past at the motel. Low, soft, directional amber light from the left. Objects in the central horizontal band, tightly framed enough to read at small scale. Restrained cinematic survival-horror still life, subtle grain, realistic scale. Opaque full bleed with no HUD, text overlay, character, enemies, gore or decorations.
